text:
Eric Pohlkamp got his first NHL point on a night when San Jose still couldn't end its slide. The Sharks, winless in five (0-5-0), came within a goal of a comeback in Dallas before falling 4-3. Pohlkamp, a 2023 pick out of Cedar Rapids who played at the University of Denver last season, assisted on Ivar Stenberg's second-period goal that cut the deficit to 3-2.

The hole was dug in the first period. The Stars scored three times in a span of about 10 minutes, and two of the goals came on the power play, from Roope Hintz and Jason Robertson. Dallas went 3 for 5 with the man advantage, while San Jose went 1 for 6. Thomas Harley, the 2019 first-round pick, added a power-play slap shot in the second and finished with a goal and two assists. Our numbers say the Stars deserved it: deserved to win, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, put Dallas at 72 percent. They also led in expected goals, a measure of chance quality, 4.59 to 3.11, and won 39 of 56 faceoffs.

San Jose made it uncomfortable anyway. Will Smith scored on the power play with 58 seconds left in the second, and Macklin Celebrini, the 2024 first overall pick, picked up three assists in 28 minutes. The Sharks managed only 0.27 expected goals in the third, though, and could not find a tying goal. San Jose now carries a five-game winless run into its next game, and it has been outscored 9-3 by Dallas in two meetings this season. The Stars, who also won the October 5 game 5-0, sweep the pair so far.
